# dsh-fa-rtl
**Right-to-left display for Persian (Farsi) chat messages in the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI.**
فارسی | English
Persian answers from the model — and your own Persian messages — render right-to-left and right-alig
ned, while English paragraphs, code blocks, and tables keep their original left-to-right layout. It
is a pure DSH plugin: no modification to the application's files, no build toolchain, nothing to con
figure after install.
## How it works
Every chat row DSH ships is laid out left-to-right (LTR); Persian text inside it is bidi-reordered b
y the Unicode algorithm, but the *base direction* stays LTR — so Persian paragraphs stay left-aligne
d and punctuation drifts to the wrong edge.
The web-standard fix is `dir="auto"`. Since plugins cannot touch the React-rendered DOM, this plugin
uses its exact CSS equivalent:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`unicode-bidi: plaintext` (CSS Writing Modes 4) lets **each text block** choose its own direction fr
om the block's first strong character — a paragraph starting with Persian renders RTL and right-alig
ns; a paragraph starting with English is unchanged. Consequences:
- Mixed answers (Persian prose + code + tables) render correctly: prose RTL, `<pre>` code deliberate

ly untouched (stays LTR), table cells per-cell, list markers flip with their list.
- The selector sc
opes only to stable `data-*` attributes that `dsh-client-ui-chat` emits on its flow items (`data-cha
t-flow-kind`, `data-chat-group-part`, `data-turn-process-answer`). Build-time hashed class names are
never referenced, so the plugin survives UI updates. If an attribute ever changes, the CSS simply s
tops matching — it cannot break the app.
## Install
Requires DSH ≥ 0.2.0-rc.2 with a web composition (`desktop` or `web` profile). Any Chromium/Electron
≥ 0.2.0-rc.2 with a web composition (`desktop` or `web` profile). Any Chromium/Electron ≥ 105 works.
### From the DSH Web UI
Open the **Plugins** page in the sidebar and install the bundle from this repository's GitHub addres
s (`github:mehdinikzad68/dsh-fa-rtl`). Installation runs `pnpm` in the profile directory and enables
the bundle by default.
### From the CLI

Installation normally enables the bundle automatically; if not, toggle it on from the Plugins page.
Restart the app once if your profile applies patches only at startup.
### From an agent session
Ask the agent to use the `plugin_manager` tool with action `install_bundle` and the GitHub spec. Eac
h management call requires your approval.

## Verify
1. Ask the model something in Persian — the Persian text renders RTL and right-aligned; numbers and

punctuation sit correctly; code stays LTR.
2. Browser console (or DevTools) shows: `[dsh-fa-rtl] act

ive — Persian chat text now renders right-to-left`
3. `<head>` contains a `<style data-plugin="dsh-f

a-rtl">` tag.
4. Settings → Plugins shows no synchronization error for the bundle.
## Uninstall
Remove the bundle from the Plugins page or with `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-fa-rtl` (
installed route), or delete the `fa-rtl` insert block from `cordis.patch.yml` (local route). The mod
ule system removes the plugin's stylesheet when the entry is disabled.

## Extend
- Want more surfaces RTL (e.g. `ask_user_question` cards)? Widen the scope selector list in `lib/cli

ent.js` and save — HMR hot-swaps the bundle, or restart once.
- Want *forced* RTL for everything (ev
en English text)? Replace `unicode-bidi: plaintext` with `direction: rtl` in the same file.
## Known limitations
- A paragraph that *starts* with a Latin word (e.g. «VS Code را نصب کن») resolves LTR in auto mode —
the same behavior as `dir="auto"` everywhere on the web; the Persian runs inside still order correc

tly.
- Overflowing wide tables keep their physical margins; very wide Persian tables may align sligh

tly differently.
- Question cards (`ask_user_question`) and some side bars are intentionally out of

ly.
- Question cards (`ask_user_question`) and some side bars are intentionally out of scope for v1.
